title: Visual architecture map: interactive graph rendering of components and dependencies
description:
Sutra has all the data for a visual architecture map (components, deps, call graphs, symbol health) but zero visual output. Design an interactive graph frontend — likely ReactFlow or similar — that renders sutra's component/dependency graph as an explorable canvas.

Key design questions to brainstorm:
- What graph layers to expose? Component-level (coarse) vs file-level vs symbol-level (fine) — probably tiered drill-down
- Layout algorithms for graphs with thousands of nodes (lore-map sidesteps this by having ≤7 top-level nodes; sutra can't)
- Delivery model: standalone web server? MCP-served? VS Code webview? CLI-launched browser?
- Data flow: live from sutra's SQLite snapshot, or exported static JSON?
- What edges to show: imports, calls, containment? Toggleable?
- Filtering/focus: show blast radius of a selected symbol, highlight hot paths, color by health score
- Prior art: lore-map (ReactFlow, ~7 coarse nodes, LLM-generated), Sourcegraph, CodeSee, Dependency Cruiser

Inspired by lore-map's visualization layer, but built on sutra's deterministic, symbol-level data rather than LLM-generated coarse graphs.
execution_record: Brainstormed via vidhi-brainstorm. Key decisions: Flutter desktop app (Linux-first), direct SQLite read (no server), breadcrumb drill-down (components → files → symbols), three layout engines (force-directed default, layered, circle packing), toggleable overlays for constraints/conventions/health/hotspots. PRD captured in thread/1.
